   The Pearl River appeared to crest at just under 37 feet (11.3 meters), 
Reeves said. It is forecast to fall below major flood stage at 36 feet (11 
meters) around midnight Tuesday, although more problems could arise if rains in 
the next few days are heavier than forecast.

   "We as a state are not in the clear yet," Reeves said.

   The Pearl's highest recorded crest was 43.2 feet on April 17, 1979. The 
second-highest level occurred May 5, 1983, when the river rose to 39.58 feet.

   Reeves thanked residents for heeding evacuation orders. Only 16

left in driveways. 

   The momentary break in the rain enabled water levels at the Barnett 
Reservoir upriver of the capital to stabilize, but officials repeated their 
warnings to pay attention to evacuation orders, check on road closures before 
traveling and stay off any flooded roads.

   Mississippi emergency management officials said Sunday that they had 
received preliminary damage reports from 11 counties connected with the severe 
weather that began on Feb. 10.

   River gauges in four states from South Carolina west to Mississippi are 
reporting moderate flooding, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

   Forecasters predict more rain across the Southeast this week. It shouldn't 
be as heavy as previous weeks, but with lakes and reservoirs nearing capacity, 
it won't take a deluge to require authorities to release more water.

   Dramatic video posted by a Tennessee fire department showed the impact near 
Savannah: Two houses tumbled down  a bluff over the Tennessee River, while many 
others have been swamped to their rooftops, as entire neighborhoods disappear 
in muddy water below the Tennessee Valley Authority's Pickwick Reservoir. 

   Dozens of other homes in more low-lying areas were swamped, the department's 
drone video showed.

   "It absolutely kills you, knowing that" houses are getting destroyed

way to move this water downstream with the least impact. They feel it. I feel 

   February's rains have been "400 percent of normal, and we have more coming 
in this week. It's kind of a never-ending battle," Hopson added. 

   The Pickwick is the next-to-last dam in the TVA's system, and all the water 
from a river basin stretching into Virginia and Georgia has to flow through it 
before reaching the Ohio River and then the Mississippi. Water levels behind 
upstream tributary dams used to contain the flooding have risen as much as 40 
feet this month, but even then, the Pickwick was releasing 2.36 million gallons 
per second Monday, down only slightly from 2.5 million gallons per second 
Sunday night, Hopson said.

River and its thousands of miles of tributaries and streams," Hopson said.

10 Reasons why cats are smarter than dogs

There are several theories as to why cats are considered smarter than dogs. One theory posits that cats are better at problem-solving than dogs because they are timid and cautious by nature. This means that they are more likely to think through a problem before acting, while dogs are more likely to act first and think later. Another theory suggests that cats are smarter than dogs because they are more independent and self-sufficient. This means that they are less likely to rely on humans for guidance and are more likely to figure things out for themselves. Additionally, cats are known for their excellent memory and their ability to learn new tricks and behaviors. Finally, cats have been shown to be more sensitive to environmental cues than dogs, which means that they are better able to adapt to new situations.

How much smarter are cats than dogs?

There is no definitive answer to this question as it depends on a number of factors, including the individual animal’s intelligence, breed, and even age. However, some experts believe that, on average, cats are more intelligent than dogs. This is because cats have a larger brain-to-body ratio than dogs, meaning they have more brain power relative to their size. Additionally, cats have more neurons in their cerebral cortex (the part of the brain responsible for higher-order cognitive functions) than dogs.

1. Cats have a much better memory than dogs. They can remember things for up to 16 hours, while dogs can only remember things for up to 2 hours.

2. Cats are better at problem solving than dogs. They can figure out how to open doors, cabinets, and other things that dogs can’t.

3. Cats are better at using their senses than dogs. They can see in the dark and hear high-pitched sounds that dogs can’t.

4. Cats are better at communication than dogs. They can meow to communicate their needs, while dogs can only bark.

5. Cats are cleaner than dogs. They groom themselves regularly, while dogs need to be bathed.

6. Cats don’t need as much exercise as dogs. They can be content to stay indoors, while dogs need to go for walks or runs.

7. Cats are more independent than dogs. They don’t need to be with people as much as dogs do.

8. Cats are less likely to get sick than dogs. They don’t catch as many diseases as dogs do.

9. Cats live longer than dogs. The average lifespan of a cat is 14 years, while the average lifespan of a dog is only 10 years.

Q: Is 987,543,247 an Even Number?

 A: No, the number 987,543,247 is not an even number - it is an odd number.

How is 987,543,247 not an even number?

An even number is any integer (a whole number) that can be divided by 2. If you can cleanly divide a number by 2, the number is even. If you divide by 2 and there is a remainder left, then the number is odd.

Let's try that calculation...

987,543,247 ÷ 2 = 493,771,623.5

Notice the number is not a whole number and has a remainder (the .5)? That means the number is an odd number.

How to identify an even number without a calculator

Any number that ends in 2, 4, 6 or 8 is even. If the number is larger than 10, if it ends in 0 it is also an even number. They are even because they can be divided by 2 evenly.

We first want to find the whole number, and to do this we divide the numerator by the denominator. Since we are only interested in whole numbers, we ignore any numbers to the right of the decimal point.
